items.title: Tim Ries interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 19, 2022
items.q: to play music to that level like Elvin Jones or Jack DeJohnette or Miles Davis or Wayne Shorter or Duke Ellington, you have to be unbelievably brilliant to be able to play at that level that brilliantly.

ctx.x: directions simply the product of your big ears, your curiosity, or are they sometimes directed by economics, what’s happening in the business now? I mean what goes into these projects, which I imagine are never easy — I want to assemble this group of people and do this particular kind of music?

It’s never easy and I don’t ever think about the money part of it. And I probably should if I was more wise that way I would maybe get a lot more money but all of the projects are just like this is what I want to do and somehow I’m going to make it happen somehow, like the “Jazz Griots” is just like this project with Jordan Walker-Pearlman and he’s a film director in L.A. And only because I was on a flight going from New York to L.A. I was sitting next to a gentleman who is a producer and he’s a lawyer but he’s…

they’re just like being nice. Turns out he was being nice and he got back to New York, sure enough I met with this director Jordan Walker-Pearlman. He goes, “I hear you have ideas for movies.” And I actually took out a list of like ten ideas. And he looks at these ideas and he goes, “I think we should do that one first, what do you think?” I said, “Yeah.” He goes, “Okay let’s start.” And believe it or not we filmed already two and then right before the pandemic so we’re trying to now start again. But it’s my idea…
